skill.name: fiftyone-develop-plugin
skill.description: Helps build custom FiftyOne operators and panels, from requirements through local testing, including Python, React, secrets, and external API patterns.
skill.summary: Guides creation, installation, and testing of custom FiftyOne plugin operators and panels.
skill.author: AdonaiVera

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by markdown code fences, documentation links, standard FiftyOne plugin paths, and placeholder secret examples. One medium issue remains: the label exporter example writes to a caller-supplied output path without path validation. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve the path, reject traversal or sensitive locations, and ask before overwriting existing files.

remediation.issue: External API examples need clearer privacy guidance
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to use trusted endpoints and avoid sending private file paths without consent.

remediation.issue: Secret handling expectations could be explicit
remediation.suggestion: State that generated plugins must use ctx.secrets or environment variables and never hardcode credentials.

content.value_statement: FiftyOne plugin development can be hard to structure correctly. This skill guides design, code generation, local installation, testing, and iteration.
actual_capabilities: Guides requirements gathering for new FiftyOne plugins.
Defines file structures for Python operators, Python panels, and JavaScript panels.
Provides examples for manifests, operator registration, panel configuration, and input types.
Explains local installation and testing with the FiftyOne App.
Shows patterns for secrets, external APIs, delegated execution, and output displays.
limitations: It does not include a runnable scaffolding command or generator script.
Examples require FiftyOne, Python, and sometimes Node.js to be installed.
External API integrations require user-provided credentials and endpoint review.
It cannot validate the final plugin without access to the local FiftyOne App.

use_cases.title: Create Dataset Operators
use_cases.description: Design a FiftyOne operator that processes selected samples, accepts user inputs, and returns clear results.

use_cases.title: Build Review Panels
use_cases.description: Plan a panel that summarizes dataset fields, displays charts, and supports sample review workflows.

use_cases.title: Prototype API Integrations
use_cases.description: Add a user-approved external service call with declared secrets, progress reporting, and local testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Operator
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a FiftyOne operator plugin for selected samples. Ask the required questions before writing files.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Python Panel
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a plan for a Python panel that shows dataset statistics and refreshes when the view changes.

prompt_templates.title: Add an API Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a FiftyOne operator that calls my approved API endpoint with a declared secret and stores returned labels.

prompt_templates.title: Design a React Panel Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a JavaScript FiftyOne panel with React state, selected sample actions, local build steps, and testing checks.

output_examples.input: I need an operator that exports labels from selected samples.
output_examples.output: A plugin plan with required files, operator inputs, export behavior, local install steps, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: I want a panel that shows label distributions for the current view.
output_examples.output: A panel design covering state updates, field selection, chart data, refresh behavior, and testing in the app.

output_examples.input: Connect my dataset workflow to an approved image analysis API.
output_examples.output: An integration outline with secret declaration, endpoint review, request flow, progress reporting, and error handling.

best_practices: Ask clarifying questions before creating plugin files.
Confirm plugin type, data flow, and secret needs before coding.
Install and test the plugin locally after each meaningful change.
anti_patterns: Building a plugin before the user approves the scope.
Hardcoding secrets or service credentials in plugin files.
Skipping local installation and FiftyOne App verification.

faq.question: What can this skill build?
faq.answer: It helps design and generate FiftyOne operators, Python panels, and JavaScript panels with matching plugin metadata.

faq.question: Does it install FiftyOne for me?
faq.answer: No. It assumes FiftyOne is installed and uses local commands only when the user approves.

faq.question: Can it connect to external APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide API integrations, but credentials and endpoints must come from the user.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready plugins?
faq.answer: It provides strong starting patterns. You still need local testing, security review, and project-specific validation.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Python operators, Python panels, and React-based JavaScript panels.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
